mapInfo.title: What is VIGIL Map?
mapInfo.desc: This interactive map visualizes the outputs of our machine learning pipeline across K'Bang and Mang Yang districts, Gia Lai Province, as translated from satellite data into actionable risk intelligence. Each 1 km² grid cell is assigned a deforestation risk probability generated by our Random Forest model, color-coded across three tiers: high risk (>0.7), medium risk (0.4–0.7), and low risk (<0.4). Warning zones highlight the top 10% highest-risk cells, providing forest rangers and conservation planners with a prioritized, data-driven foundation for patrol deployment. As a next step, we are expanding our dataset to scale this map to full national coverage across Vietnam in 2026. *Note: These outputs represent pilot model predictions and serve as prioritization zones — not legal proof of forest loss.

about.hero_title: Join VIGIL in protecting our forests!
about.brand_story_subtitle: The echo from the great forest and the promise of Digital Guardians
about.brand_story_p1: It all started not from a lab or textbooks, but from our field trip to Cuc Phuong National Park.
about.brand_story_p2: Amidst the tranquil ancient forest, real-world data on the rapid pace of forest degradation, biodiversity imbalance, and threats to wildlife gave our group of young friends pause. Looking back at the devastating storms and landslides occurring across Vietnam with increasing frequency, we realized: Severe natural disasters are the direct consequence when protective forests can no longer shield us.
about.brand_story_p3: Witnessing this reality, we decided we had to do something to protect these primary forests instead of merely regretting their loss.
about.brand_story_p4: That is why VIGIL was born. Woven from the daring spirit of youth, VIGIL acts as a silent "Digital Guardian" keeping watch over the vast forests. The project transforms invisible satellite data streams into precise early warnings and concrete on-the-ground action. We want to prove that: Artificial intelligence is not just emotionless algorithms. When guided by a love for nature, AI becomes a powerful tool to protect every green patch of our country.
about.trip_1_desc: Started with a volunteer trip to Ninh Binh in 2025, the experience became a turning point that completely shifted the founding team’s perspective on nature conservation. Working alongside forest rangers and conservation organizations, the team took part in forest restoration by planting trees in degraded areas, caring for caring for fortunate rescued wildlife, surveying forest conditions, and learning firsthand about deforestation hotspots and the challenges faced by those responsible for protecting them. Immersing themselves in the physical work of regenerating barren lands and tending to rescued animals, the founders gained a direct look at the alarming numbers behind the rapid loss of primary forests and the harsh reality of poaching shared by local experts.
about.trip_2_desc: Drawing from satellite data that records decades of forest canopy changes, the team collected and processed massive multi-source datasets to develop a predictive deforestation risk map, selecting Gia Lai province as the pilot area. By analyzing over 6,000 1-km² grid cells through a machine learning pipeline, the map can accurately identify and isolate high-risk zones well before any actual loss occurs. The goal of the map is to place this strategic tool directly into the hands of environmental NGOs and forest rangers. Doing so will support proactive forecasting and the development of active conservation strategies, ultimately minimizing response times and ensuring swift interventions at violation hotspots.
about.trip_3_desc: After completing the deforestation risk map from satellite data, the VIGIL team traveled to Gia Lai for three days to ground-truth what the model had predicted against conditions on the ground. Working alongside local forest rangers and provincial authorities, the team surveyed areas flagged as high-risk by the map, investigated the specific causes behind each zone of forest loss, and collected additional field data to deepen the research pipeline. Alongside the technical work, the team participated in tree-planting activities at sites currently undergoing restoration and spent time in conversation with local communities about livelihoods built around the forest. The experience opened a dimension that satellite data alone cannot capture: forests are not only a resource to be protected but the economic foundation of entire communities, and any conservation strategy that aims to last must integrate sustainable livelihoods and green tourism into its core design.

publication.hero_subtitle: Explore the technical foundations and AI methodologies behind VIGIL's early warning system.
publication.authors: Authors: Pham Duy Long | Nguyen Duc Anh | Do Nhat Quang | Nguyen Vu Huy | Dam Anh Thu | Tran Dang An
publication.abstract_p1: The core scientific foundation of Project VIGIL bridges the gap in proactive deforestation risk modeling in Southeast Asia with an interpretable machine learning framework, predicting risk at a 1 km² resolution in Gia Lai, Vietnam.
publication.abstract_p2: Using a pilot study across K'Bang and Mang Yang districts, we integrate multi-source data from Google Earth Engine, including Hansen Global Forest Change, Global Forest Watch alerts, Sentinel-2 spectral indices, topographic features, and road network proximity (OpenStreetMap), to build a structured feature table across 6,000+ grid cells.
publication.abstract_p3: We evaluate three modeling approaches: a baseline risk score, logistic regression, and random forest. Our random forest model achieves an AUC of 0.942, while logistic regression provides interpretable insights into key risk drivers such as proximity to roads and vegetation condition.
publication.abstract_p4: This platform serves as a pilot implementation of a scalable framework for national forest-risk monitoring in Vietnam. This research has been accepted for publication in MDPI Remote Sensing (Q1, Scopus-indexed), with print scheduled for September 2026.
publication.methodology_p1: 01. Multi-Source Data Integration. Our pipeline leverages the computational power of Google Earth Engine to harmonize disparate geospatial datasets. The core challenge addressed is the alignment of heterogeneous spatial and temporal resolutions—ranging from 10m Sentinel-2 bands to 30m SRTM terrain data—into a standardized 1 km resolution analytical master table.
publication.datasets_p1: All inputs are public datasets accessed and processed within Google Earth Engine (GEE). The pipeline integrates forest baseline and loss history (Hansen), terrain (SRTM), rainfall (CHIRPS), and optical predictors from Sentinel-2 for the 2023 reporting year. Geospatial processing involves defining boundaries, generating a 1 km grid, computing outcome labels, and aggregating predictor layers.
publication.results_p1: Both logistic regression and random forest substantially improve discrimination relative to the baseline score. Logistic regression coefficients indicate the direction of association between standardized predictors and deforestation risk, while random forest feature importance highlights predictors that strongly contribute to the model’s decisions (achieving an AUC of 0.942).
publication.future_p1: Future work should add time-based validation using loss_first_year to evaluate early-warning behavior and incorporate additional predictors such as distance to roads or settlements, protected areas, land tenure, and proximity to agriculture.
